transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-10
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Marta Lopez (Redwood CSM), Dana Morales (Head of ML, NimbleGrid), Evan Zhou (Platform Eng), Priya Singh (Security Lead), Leo Grant (SRE)

Summary:
Quick weekly POC sync focused on improving KV/prefix cache hit-rate, evaluating prompt-reuse strategy at production traffic, and aligning on security artifacts and next steps for a small prod canary. Some noisy audio; transcription imperfect in spots.

Topics covered:
- Latest hit-rate numbers and where misses cluster
- Eviction strategy and TTLs for session tokens
- Prompt normalization / canonicalization approach to increase prefix reuse
- Safety/security / KMS / audit log gating for pilot
- Canary rollout plan and success metrics

Action items (brief):
- See metadata action_items

Transcript:
[00:00] Avery Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll get started. Quick check, audio good on your side?
[00:12] Dana Morales: Yep, good here. Thanks Avery.
[00:15] Ravi Patel: Morning, hi all. I'll jump into the hit-rate slide first.
[00:20] [Screen share starts]
[00:25] Ravi Patel: So last 72 hours we've got overall KV hit-rate at 42%, prefix reuse about 28% if we apply the normalization pipeline we discussed. You can see the spike on weekdays at 10:00 UTC when the bot-driven workflows start.
[00:40] Leo Grant: That 42% is across all sessions or only warmed nodes?
[00:45] Ravi Patel: That's cluster-wide. Warmed nodes show about 57% but the cold-path is killing the aggregate. We also saw a small regression on Tuesday when your deployment changed the prompt preamble.
[01:05] Dana Morales: Right we pushed a small logging header change, so that explains a lot. Is that header included in the prefix key?
[01:13] Ravi Patel: Yes currently our hash includes the first 120 tokens. We can add a canonicalization step to strip headers and timestamps which should bump prefix matches.
[01:25] Dana Morales: Great, that's high priority for us.
[01:30] Priya Singh: Quick sec, on the security side we need to know if canonicalization happens client-side or server-side. We prefer server-side in Redwood Private because we don't want raw payload in logs.
[01:42] Avery Chen: Good point. For Private customers we can do canonicalization in the runtime before any persistent logging happens — we can also keep the raw input only in memory and redact before write.
[01:55] Priya Singh: Can you point us to your KMS integration docs again? We need to map key rotation rules to our audit requirements.
[02:02] Marta Lopez: I'll drop the KMS appendix and the SOC2 excerpt after the call. Link's in the handoff notes.
[02:10] Evan Zhou: Back on hit rates, one question: are we seeing misses due to tokenization differences? We have multi-lingual traffic with some zero-width characters that may affect the key.
[02:21] Ravi Patel: Good catch. Tokenization drift is a big factor. We run a normalization pass but it doesn't handle ZWJ/ZWNJ characters well today. We'll add that to the pre-processing.
[02:35] [Timestamp 00:03:00] Dana Morales: For the prefix reuse strategy, could you explain the delta between prefix matching and KV cache hits? I recall they're related but not identical.
[02:45] Ravi Patel: Sure. Prefix reuse is an application-layer pattern where the prefix of the prompt matches an existing cached KV entry so the model can resume from a hot KV state. KV hit-rate is broader — it includes exact key matches for session-level cache and prefetch entries. So high prefix reuse usually drives KV hits but you can have KV hits without prefix reuse, for example if you prefetch a completion.
[03:10] Leo Grant: Does Redwood do prefetching automatically or do we need to configure it?
[03:14] Avery Chen: We have an adaptive prefetcher we can enable for Dedicated and Private. It learns traffic patterns and pre-warms hot keys. For hosted tiers we do conservative prefetching by default.
[03:28] Evan Zhou: Can we tune the TTL per cohort? Our traffic has 3 main cohorts — search, chat, and longform — would like shorter TTL for longform.
[03:40] Ravi Patel: Yes, we support cohort-based TTLs in the config. We can demo a sample config that sets chat TTL to 45s, search 12s, longform 180s, etc.
[03:55] [Small crosstalk]
[04:00] Priya Singh: On audit logs — are cached keys obfuscated? We need to ensure PII isn't written to logs.
[04:07] Ravi Patel: By default keys are hashed with HMAC before being stored; we can also add deterministic redaction for known PII patterns. For Private deployments you can plug your HSM/KMS.
[04:20] Priya Singh: Ok that helps.
[04:25] Dana Morales: A concrete question — what's the expected uplift after we apply header stripping and the extra normalization? Any ballpark?
[04:33] Ravi Patel: Early tests on similar traffic bumped prefix reuse from 28% to about 38% and KV hit-rate from 42% to ~52% — so 8–12% absolute uplift typically, sometimes more if prompts are very repetitive.
[04:48] Dana Morales: That's promising.
[04:52] Evan Zhou: Let's talk about eviction. We saw a sharp drop when traffic spiked, suggesting thrash. What eviction strategy are you recommending? LRU, LFU, or adaptive?
[05:02] Ravi Patel: For large multi-tenant pools we prefer an adaptive hybrid: LFU with decaying counters tuned by cohort, plus a small LRU fast-evict buffer for burst isolation. That reduces thrash compared to naive LRU.
[05:18] Leo Grant: Can we run simulation of our traffic to validate?
[05:22] Avery Chen: Yes — Ravi will run an eviction sim with your corpus. We'll need a 1% sample of anonymized prompts and p95 length distribution.
[05:33] Dana Morales: We'll provide that.
[05:36] [Timestamp 00:06:00] Marta Lopez: Quick note — there was one customer-level regression we flagged last week when the model roll forward bumped tokenization model, which changed hot key distribution. That drift is something we can monitor in the Console.
[05:52] Ravi Patel: Right, drift detection will be in the metrics. We'll create an alert for >5% drop in rolling hit-rate over 1h.
[06:02] Dana Morales: Can you show the dashboard layout for those alerts?
[06:06] Ravi Patel: I'll share a template.
[06:09] [Screen share stops]
[06:12] Evan Zhou: About the canary — our constraint window is only 3 hours during low traffic, can we do an incremental canary that ramps up for a day instead?
[06:22] Avery Chen: Yes, we can do a gradual ramp with traffic steering. For safety we'll start with a 0.5% shard, then 2%, 10% over the day. If stability is good we continue.
[06:34] Priya Singh: We will need an incident contact list and rollback runbook in case the KV layer behaves badly.
[06:40] Marta Lopez: We'll attach a rollback playbook and contact list in the next steps.
[06:45] [Timestamp 00:08:00] Dana Morales: One operational question: what does warmup look like? If we prefetch keys, how long to reach steady-state?
[06:55] Ravi Patel: Warmup depends on traffic shape. For chat-heavy workloads we often see steady-state after 30–90 minutes of sustained traffic; for search it can be faster. Prefetching plus initial canonicalization speeds this up a lot.
[07:12] Leo Grant: Do you persist session snapshots across restarts? We had restarts overnight and lost some warm KV states.
[07:18] Ravi Patel: Session snapshots can be optionally persisted to local SSD or external Redis as a tiered cache; that prevents cold restarts. For Dedicated we usually enable local snapshotting.
[07:28] Evan Zhou: Cost question — how much additional egress or storage do snapshots add?
[07:33] Avery Chen: Small relative to total token cost, but depends on snapshot frequency. We can provide a cost estimate after we see your snapshot size distribution.
[07:44] [Timestamp 00:10:00] Dana Morales: Ok, on prompt reuse canonicalization — what rules do you propose? Lowercasing, whitespace normalization, header stripping, remove tracking tokens?
[07:54] Ravi Patel: Start conservative: strip known headers/timestamps, trim whitespace, normalize unicode (NFKC), remove common tracking tokens. Avoid aggressive semantic normalization that could change model output.
[08:08] Dana Morales: Makes sense. We'll provide a list of things to strip.
[08:12] [Pause]
[08:20] Priya Singh: Security checklist: SSO/SAML for Console, RBAC for key material, KMS integration, SOC2 export — can you confirm which of these are available in the Private package?
[08:30] Marta Lopez: Private includes SSO/SAML, RBAC, KMS/HSM integration, and audit logs export. We'll send the feature matrix.
[08:38] Priya Singh: And log retention controls? We need 7 years for some partners.
[08:43] Marta Lopez: Retention is configurable in Private, but long-term archive may require extra storage fees — we'll call that out.
[08:49] [Timestamp 00:12:00] Evan Zhou: One more technical nit — does the runtime risk leaking prompt prefixes into the request traces? We want to avoid that.
[08:56] Ravi Patel: Traces can be configured to omit raw prompt text; we only trace hash keys by default for high-cardinality fields.
[09:05] Dana Morales: Great.
[09:10] [Timestamp 00:14:00] Ravi Patel: Ok, quick demo idea. We're going to run a prefetch tuning job that simulates your morning spike with your anonymized 1% corpus. It will produce: heatmap, hit-rate before/after, and eviction churn graphs. We'll hand that over as a short report.
[09:25] Dana Morales: That report will be useful. Can you also include top-50 prefixes that cause misses?
[09:31] Ravi Patel: Yep will include top-50.
[09:33] Leo Grant: On metrics, can we get token-level cost estimate per optimization? For example, if we move from 42% to 52% hit-rate what's the cost delta?
[09:43] Avery Chen: We have a unit-economics calculator in the Console. We'll run a model with your cost inputs and share a cost-savings estimate.
[09:50] [Timestamp 00:16:00] Priya Singh: Any concerns about GDPR/residency for using hosted inference? We might need EU region only for some customers.
[09:58] Marta Lopez: We can pin region for Dedicated and Private. Hosted supports EU-region tenancy but for strict residency we recommend Private.
[10:06] Dana Morales: Let's plan for Dedicated for our EU customers.
[10:10] Evan Zhou: Is there a checklist for Dedicated onboarding?
[10:13] Marta Lopez: Yes, we'll share an onboarding checklist — network reqs, firewall rules, RH versions, and a sample infra template.
[10:20] [Timestamp 00:18:00] Dana Morales: Can we add a metric for customer-facing latency percentiles when prefetch is enabled?
[10:27] Ravi Patel: Absolutely, we can instrument p50/p95/p99 and show delta when prefetching. We'll also highlight any tail amplification.
[10:34] Dana Morales: Good.
[10:38] [Timestamp 00:20:00] Avery Chen: Let's do a quick recap and next steps.
[10:42] Avery Chen: Action items: Ravi to run eviction sim and export prefix heatmap by 2027-02-16; Evan to provide anonymized 1% prompt corpus and p95 distribution by 2027-02-13; Marta to share KMS/SOC2 artifacts and Dedicated onboarding checklist by 2027-02-12.
[10:58] Dana Morales: That works. Also please include the cost-savings calc.
[11:03] Avery Chen: Noted. We'll also propose a canary ramp schedule (0.5% -> 2% -> 10%).
[11:09] Priya Singh: We'll review the rollback playbook and confirm contacts.
[11:13] Marta Lopez: I'll follow up with calendar invites for the canary window and attach docs.
[11:18] Evan Zhou: Thanks everyone.
[11:20] Avery Chen: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the report and configs.
[11:24] [Call ends]

Notes about transcription imperfections:
- "KV" sometimes transcribed as "K V" or "K-V cash" in the raw output.
- Model roll-forward mentioned as tokenization model bump — original term may have been "tokenizer model".
- Some proper nouns (e.g., internal feature flags) may be slightly off.
